title: Routing & Auth Quick Pulse — notes and action items
content:
Attendees: Asha (owner), Miguel, Evan, Priya, Liam, + brief drop-ins from SRE (Nina) and Product (Theo)

Meeting length: 35m (quick pulse, not full sync)
Context: follow-up from July planning board — focused on routing policy edge cases, auth token rotation regressions, and quota accounting drift seen in yesterday's nightly job.

Agenda:
- Quick surface of incidents/alerts (2m)
- Routing policy fallback behaviour for shared vs. dedicated pools (8m)
- Auth token rotation and 401 spike root-cause (10m)
- Quotas accounting drift & mitigation (8m)
- Actions / owners / due dates (5m)

Notes and discussion:
1) Incidents/alerts
- Nightly job reported ~1.4% user-facing 429s between 02:00-02:12 UTC. SRE traced to quota recalculation window when batch window moved. Related to RED-1742.
- No customer escalation yet but product requested mitigation for canary users.

2) Routing policy fallback (Miguel)
- Current behavior: when preferred dedicated pool is saturated, requests fall back to a compatible hosted variant; if none available, they queue. Observed that routing prefers lower-cost variants but sometimes routes to higher-latency region when cheaper local pool has intermittent errors.
- Proposed: add a short-circuit that prefers same-region higher-cost pool over cross-region higher-latency fallback. This would reduce tail latency for internal SLAs.
- Tradeoffs: cross-region bandwidth cost vs. latency SLA. Product is okay with temporary cost bump for canary group.
- Decision (tentative): implement region-aware preference flag on RoutePolicy with a 10s TTL. Start as feature-flagged for canary only.

3) Auth token rotation spike (Priya)
- Root cause: token rotation worker batch size doubled in last deploy (accidental config change in pr#512). Rotation created short window where legacy tokens were considered expired by some proxies leading to 401 surge.
- Short-term: revert the rotation worker to previous batch size (PR ready). Priya to hotfix by EOD.
- Long-term: add canary rollout for worker config changes and add metric: token-refresh-loss-rate per-proxy.

4) Quotas accounting drift (Evan + Liam)
- Drift summary: usage totals in nightly aggregation were ~0.7% higher than live counters for a subset of customers. Root cause likely double-counting when requests retried after transient failures (retries were recorded on both original and retry paths).
- Quick mitigations discussed: (a) idempotency keys for user-level accounting (requires client adoption), (b) server-side dedupe in aggregation window (cheap, immediate), (c) mark-and-sweep reconciliation daily.
- Decided: implement server-side dedupe within aggregation pipeline for next nightly job to stop immediate drift. Then schedule design for idempotency keys for Q3.

Decisions summary:
- Add region-aware preference flag to RoutePolicy, feature-flagged for canary (owner: Miguel, due: 2026-07-15).
- Hotfix token rotation batch size revert (owner: Priya, due: 2026-07-08 EOD).
- Add server-side dedupe in quota aggregation pipeline (owner: Evan, due: 2026-07-10).
- Observe nightly job run post-dedupe and report back (owner: Liam, due: 2026-07-11).

Action items (owner | due | status):
- Miguel | 2026-07-15 | TODO — prototype RoutePolicy flag + unit tests + toggle in console. Link: github PR stub.
- Priya | 2026-07-08 | IN_PROGRESS — revert rotation worker config, patch and deploy to staging, smoke test. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/512
- Evan | 2026-07-10 | TODO — add dedupe step to nightly aggregation (suggested: memory-bounded bloom filter keyed by request-id for window).
- Liam | 2026-07-11 | TODO — run reconciliation and prepare short report (include top 10 customers affected).
- Nina (SRE) | 2026-07-09 | TODO — add alert runbook note for quota-drift class and create a Grafana dashboard panel showing live vs nightly totals.

Blockers and open questions:
- Does adding a region-aware preference create any unintended capacity pressure in target regions during rain (multi-customer spikes)? Need capacity simulation. (Action: Miguel + Platform simulation team, due 2026-07-14)
- Client adoption of idempotency keys is slow; can we provide SDK helpers to generate and attach keys? (Product + DevX follow-up)
- How to express the RoutePolicy TTL in existing UI? UX discussion needed (Product).

Notes-to-self / rough ideas (informal):
- Consider adding a lightweight 'route-eval' harness that replays a day's routing decisions in a staging model to validate fallback changes before rollout. Might live under control-plane/tools/route-sim.
- For quota dedupe, test with synthetic high-retry workloads to validate false-positive tolerances (bloom filter sizing).
- Put a short note in the July weekly exec sync about the rotation incident and mitigation (two sentences).

Parking lot (items not for this quick pulse):
- Revisit global vs. regional capacity tiering for enterprise customers.
- Explore a 'grace window' for token acceptance during rotation to minimize 401s across proxies.

Quick metrics snapshot (rough):
- 429 spike: 1.4% of requests in 12m window (02:00-02:12 UTC) — mostly small requests to embeddings route.
- 401 spike coincident: +0.9% over baseline during rotation window.
- Quota drift: 0.7% upward on nightly aggregates for affected customers.

Next sync: regular platform standup on 2026-07-13; reconvene if hotfix escalates.

Raw notes and traces (scratch):
- Linear: RED-1742 (quota drift investigation)
- GitHub interim PR: control-plane#512 (rotation worker config)
- Slack thread: #platform-controlplane "rotation-401s" (link pinned)

End of notes.

-- Asha
